customer_question: Can we use another company's already-certified Host Subsystem QD-ID (e.g., a BlueZ-based registration) when registering our own product?
question_variants: Can we list our product against a QDID that belongs to another company's certified Host Subsystem?
Is it OK to reference a competitor's BlueZ Host Subsystem QDID for our new SIG listing?
Can we register our product using a third-party's certified component QDID without their permission?
What happens if we register using a Host Subsystem QD-ID we don't own?
Is referencing an unrelated company's certified BlueZ stack QDID for our listing technically allowed but risky?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to register their product (Host Subsystem = BlueZ) by referencing the QD-ID of another company's already-certified BlueZ Host Subsystem, without any business relationship with that company or its stack provider.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth SIG listings link a product to certified building-block components (like a Host Subsystem) via their QD-ID numbers. If you point your new product's listing at someone else's certified component without permission, your listing will show up whenever that QD-ID is searched. If the actual owner of that certified component notices, they can ask the SIG to remove your listing - even though the initial registration goes through. So while it's technically possible to file the paperwork, it creates a real risk of having your certification pulled later.
consultant_answer: Filing a new registration under your own company name that references a BlueZ Host Subsystem QD-ID certified and owned by an unrelated third party (whether self-tested or via a stack vendor's certification) is technically possible to submit, but afterward, anyone searching that QD-ID will also see your company's listing. If the Listing Owner of that QD-ID notices, they can request the SIG to cancel your registration. So although the form-level registration may succeed, there is a real subsequent risk of de-registration, and this is not recommended.
decision_logic: A product registration that references a component QD-ID (e.g., Host Subsystem) is only safe long-term if your company has a legitimate right to reference that QD-ID - either because you own it, or because you obtained it properly (e.g., purchased a certified stack from its vendor/distributor, who permits referencing their QD-ID). Referencing an unrelated party's QD-ID without permission creates a visibility link that the QD-ID owner can use to get your registration cancelled.
final_recommendation: Do not reference a third party's certified Host Subsystem QD-ID without their permission. Instead, purchase a BlueZ-based (or other) Host Subsystem stack from a licensed stack vendor/distributor, who will permit you to legitimately reference their certified QD-ID in your registration.
risk_if_done_wrong: The initial registration may go through, but if the actual owner/Listing Owner of the referenced QD-ID discovers the unauthorized reference, they can request the SIG to cancel the registration, resulting in lost certification and the need to redo the registration correctly.
